title: FDA clears AI tool for pediatric bone age assessments
key_facts: Visiana announced FDA 510(k) clearance for BoneXpert machine-learning bone age software
Cleared to support pediatric radiologists for patients aged 2 to 21 using the Greulich-Pyle method
Multicenter study at five US sites, 1,285 images, each read by four pediatric radiologists
BoneXpert error 0.55 years vs 0.76 for a single radiologist; deviations of 1.5 years or more 1.7% vs 6.4%
Runs inside the hospital network; radiologist stays responsible
In use in Europe since 2009; US release early October
quote_evidence: BoneXpert is cleared to support pediatric radiologists in assessing bone age in patients aged 2 to 21 years according to the Greulich-Pyle method.
The radiologist remains responsible for the final assessment.
BoneXpert will be released in the U.S in early October
why_it_matters_hint: Cuts reader-to-reader variation in a routine child-growth test, with a human still signing off.
notes: Radiology Business page blocked (403); assumed to cover the same Visiana BoneXpert clearance, matched by topic and date but not confirmed. ITN carries the vendor announcement. Study results are the company's.
